# Metis - alexar76/aicom GitHub Wiki

# Metis — cognition & verification tier

Metis (μῆτις) is the ecosystem's distributed cognitive layer over any LLM — Understanding Council → fail-closed confidence gate → layered Mixture-of-Agents → grounded verifier. It returns a machine-readable verification envelope (`verify_score`, `verified`, optional `needs_clarification`).

> Live demo: metis.modelmarket.dev · 3D landing: alexar76.github.io/metis · Source: github.com/alexar76/metis · PyPI: `aimarket-metis` · Factory integration: `docs/metis-integration.md`

## Why Metis matters in AICOM

Layer  | Role
--- | ---
Oracles  | Verifiable math primitives (randomness, VDF, reputation, …)
Metis  | Verifiable cognition — multi-agent reasoning + confidence gate on natural-language decisions
AI-Factory  | Produces products; optionally calls Metis on high-stakes stages (`architect`, `methodologist`)
ARGUS  | Demand-side agent; can consume Metis + MCP tools like any other host

Hard invariant: factory and Metis are independent. Missing Metis → factory runs unchanged (fail-open gate). Missing factory → Metis serves `/v1/*` normally.

## Factory integration (optional gate)

High-stakes pipeline stages can POST to Metis `/v1/verify` via `llm/metis_gate.py` (HTTP only — never imports `metis`).
    
    `export METIS_URL=https://metis.internal:8080   # default http://127.0.0.1:8080
    export AIFACTORY_METIS_GATE=auto               # auto | on | off (default auto)
    export AIFACTORY_METIS_GATE_BLOCK=0          # 1 = allow low-confidence to escalate
    `

Full env table + sequence diagrams: `docs/metis-integration.md` · RU · ES · FR · ZH

## MCP tools (Metis as consumer)

Metis agents can attach ecosystem MCP servers via presets:

Preset  | Server  | Tools
--- | --- | ---
`aimarket-oracle-gateway`  | aimarket-oracle-gateway  | 35 verifiable oracle tools
`aimarket-web`  | aimarket-mcp  | `web_fetch`, `web_search`, `metis_verify` (SSRF-hardened)
    
    `enable_mcp_tools: true
    mcp_ecosystem_presets:
      - aimarket-oracle-gateway
      - aimarket-web
    `

aimarket-mcp — shared MCP gateway (stdio on Glama, HTTP self-host). Written once; consumed by Metis, ARGUS, and any stdio/HTTP MCP host.

Metis-side doc: `metis/docs/en/ECOSYSTEM.md`

## Alien Monitor

Metis appears as the `cognition` node in Alien Monitor — live stats + in-graph chat proxied server-side (`POST /api/metis/chat`) so API keys never reach the browser.

## About

Monthly snapshots of a public transparency log covering remote MCP servers in the official registry and npm and PyPI MCP packages. The files hold the tool definitions each server served, every recorded change field by field, pattern scan matches, and advisory classifier readings. A signed manifest lists checksums so users can verify files, and the data is released under CC BY 4.0.

## What it does

The site says HISTOR reads the tool list of every remote server in the official MCP registry each day and runs each new npm and PyPI MCP package version in a sandbox. It presents its pattern matches and classifier flags as leads worth reading, not as proof that a server is malicious.

## Selling a long job

A paid call cannot wait minutes for an agent, so a GitHub activity digest is sold as two capabilities on
hub.attestedmemory.net:

  * `github.digest.order@v1` ($0.05) takes any public GitHub user or organization and 1 to 7 days, and answers at once with a job id;
  * `github.digest.result@v1` (free) returns the digest to the buyer who paid.

The first real order failed, and our own guard caused half of it. The agent read its task, including a per-job
delivery URL, then read GitHub, then tried to send the result to that URL. WARDEN treats task text as private, and
after outside text it lets no private data leave, whatever the destination. That is the rule we want for an
unattended agent; the delivery design was wrong. The other half: GitHub's 60 unauthenticated requests an hour per IP
were already spent on that host. (By what, we found later: a video worker of ours whose model calls had been failing
since September. It re-fetched GitHub every two minutes, because its failed run never saved the time.)
